Proceedings of the 31st Meeting of the National Agricultural 
Education Accreditation Board  
 
The 31st meeting of the National Agricultural Education Accreditation Board (NAEAB) was 
held under the Chairmanship of Dr. Trilochan Mohapatra, Secretary, DARE and DG, ICAR. 
Dr. R. C. Agrawal , DDG (Agril Education), ICAR in the beginning of the meeting, heartily 
welcomed the Chairman and Members of the Board with a brief achievement of the board. The 
action taken report  and agenda items along with minutes of the Appeal Committees were 
presented for discussion and consideration of the Board by Dr P.S. Pandey, Secretary, NAEAB 
and ADG (EPHS & EQR). The details are as follow: 
 
1. Confirmation of the proceedings of the 30th meeting of the NAEAB held on 17/03/2022  
 
Since there were no comments received from any members towards proceedings of the 30th 
Board meeting, therefore proceeding was approved as such. 
 
Action Taken Report 
 
1.1: Action Taken Report of JNKVV, Jabalpur  
 
 JNKVV, Jabalpur University was accredited for two years with Grade C, therefore, 
for further extension of accreditation for next three years, as per guidelines for C grade 
universities, Action Taken Report (ATR) of JNKVV, Jabalpur has been received on 
30 June 2022. It was observed that the report, on the suggestions/recommendations of 
the Board, submitted by the University was in order and most of the actions suggested 
have either been taken up, or have been initiated by the university and ATR will be 
taken up to the Mid-Term Review Committee for detailed discussion.  
 
 The university was approved for extension of accreditation for next three years with 
existing C Grade.   
 
1.2. Minutes of the Meeting of the Appeal Committee of NAEAB held on April 1, 2022 
and July 12, 2022   
 
 The minutes of the meeting of the Appeal Committee held on April 1, 2022 and  July 
12, 2022 were presented in the meeting and further approved  the recommendations. 
The case-wise approved recommendations are as follow: 
 
1.2.1. Programmes of UAS, Bengaluru: 
A. B. Sc. (Hons) Agri Business Management  
The Appeal Committee examined the appeal of UAS, Bangalore with respect to UAS, 
Bangalore for a degree programme B. Sc. (Hons) Agri Business Management. The PRT 
in its assessment had shown a clear concern that there is a shortage of core faculty to 
teach the core courses. Besides, PG and Ph. D. courses were also being run with th e 
same faculty at the time of PRT visit. It does not appear feasible to run three 
programmes with a meagre faculty of total Six as reported in the university’s Self Study 
Report (page number 59). In view of thi s, the appeal committee endorsed  the 
2 
 
observation of PRT scoring of 1 out of 4 regarding faculty. Not only this, the committee 
also had a look on other indicators and it is seen that PRT was objective and reasonable 
in its assessment. In view of this, the committee did not consider any merit in 
reconsideration of the appeal. Thus, the appeal is disposed-off accordingly. 
 
The Board considered and approved the recommendation of Appeal Committee.  
 
B. B.Tech (Biotechnology) 
Appeal committee examined the appeal submitted by UAS, Bangalore for their B.Tech 
(Biotechnology) programme of College of Agriculture, Hassan. According to PRT 
assessment, the main issue had been highlighted as inadequate faculty for the 
programme. As such, only four regular faculty and six contractual faculty was in place 
against a requirement of 34. In this programme, all the 34 faculty are placed under core 
faculty. It does not appear feasible that just a core faculty of 11 against a requirement 
of 34 can meet the teaching requirements of the course. For this parameter of facul ty 
strength, PRT awarded 1 out of 4. The appeal committee agreed with the scoring done 
by the PRT. The scoring could have been better, had the university appointed more 
faculty.  In view of this agreeing with the PRT score, the appeal committee disposed-
off the application for the reconsideration. 
 
The Board considered and approved the recommendation of Appeal Committee.  
 
1.2.2.  Parul University, Vadodara, Gujarat 
A. B. Sc. (Hons) Agriculture, College of Agriculture 
 The 5 th Deans Committee report outlines a minimum of 20 hectare of land for 
instructional farm for a college of Agriculture. Though the university has stated that it 
possesses a land of 230.75 hectare and claimed, the said land is in the name of Trustees 
who manages the Parul University. The PRT during their visit observed that they have 
limited instructional farm, in pieces, near main campus and a photocopy of MoU signed 
on 24 th October, 2021 between the Registrar and Trustees was shown to the PRT. 
Further in their appeal university cited a legal opinion that the land cannot be purchased 
by an Agricultural Education Institution. 
 The Appeal Committee had further come to know that a recently published Act {The 
Gujarat Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2020} states that the 
land for agricultural educational institutions can be purchased in the name of 
Universities/institutions. Thus, the contention of the university was not found 
admissible. 
 It is further supported by the decision of Proceeding of 28th NAEAB meeting dated 17th 
August 2021, para 4.6-point no. 6 - Universities applying for accreditation of their 
colleges should essentially have registered land in their name. Lease land may not be 
considered for accreditation. Only records issued by the local authorities regarding 
instructional farm will be considered for land verification.  
 Thus, the committee reached a conclusion that until and unless the required land is 
registered in the name of university, the case for accreditation of B.Sc. (Hons) 
Agriculture, College of Agriculture does not fulfil the minimum r equirement as laid 
down in 5 th Deans Committee Report. Thus, the case of reconsideration of the 
accreditation of B.Sc. (Hons) Agriculture was disposed-off.

1.2.3. B.Sc. (Hons) Agriculture programme, School  of Agriculture, Sri Satya Sai 
University of Technology and Medical Sciences, Sehore, M.P. 
 Appeal Committee critically examined the appeal document submitted for review 
on decision of the Board for recommendation of accreditation of B.Sc . (Hons) 
Agriculture programme. Committee discussed with Secretariat staff regarding Self 
Study Report and related PRT guidelines in this matter. Observation of Chairman, 
PRT was also recorded. University Vice -Chancellor and Dean Agriculture were 
present for discussion at length. Committee further examined the ITR form 
submitted by the University for verification of faculty and staff. 
 Based on the above, it was noted  by the committee that Appeal of Sri Satya Sai 
University of Technology and Medical Sciences, Sehore was considered for their 
B.Sc. (Hons) Agriculture, School for Agriculture. The minimum requirement of 
faculty for a batch of 60 as per 5th Deans Committee is 31. Though this university 
has got total faculty strength of 41, which is more than required, but the profile of 
faculty shows 23 of them are just M.Sc. (withou t NET). Not only this, there is no 
professor in core departments like Agronomy, Horticulture & Genetics & Plant 
Breeding. Thus, the requirement for teaching a course could be met from their 
faculty strength, but not on quality parameters in view of their qualifications. 
 Besides this, the university has submitted ITR forms for 10 faculty (for last 3 years) 
and 11 faculty have ITR for 2 years. It has come to the notice of Appeal Committee 
that conduct of practical for 1 hour duration, which does not meet Deans 
Committee regulations. In view of the requirement not being met on account of 
faculty qualifications, ITR forms, practical not conducted as per Deans Committee 
regulation, the Appeal Committee agreed with the rec ommendation of PRT and 
disposed-off appeal for reconsideration. 
 
1.2.4. B.Sc. (Hons) Agriculture, School of Agricultural Sciences, Jaipur National 
University, Jaipur  
Examination of documents and discussion by Appeal Committee : Appeal 
Committee examined the Appeal document submitted by the University, Self-Study 
Report, PRT report, additional documents submitted by the University , especially, 
ITR forms, land records and held discussion with PRT Chairman, Member Secretary 
and University Vice Chancellor/Rector (physically present). Appeal Committee 
noted that University has been maintaining ITR forms of about 19 Faculty and 
another faculty are recently appointed. Further, University presented the sale deed 
document of about 6 ha land available for the programme adjacent to university 
quarters. In addition to that some land is also available on lease and contract from 
the adjoining farmers. The issue of other requisite instructional facilities available at 
the instructional farm could only be verified physically.  
 
4 
 
Recommendation of the Appeal Committee: Considering the reports, documents 
and discussion mentioned above, appeal committee recommended considering 
accreditation of the B. Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture programme initially for a period of 
one year, starting from the date of Board’s approval. Mid-Term Review Committee 
of the Board will further physically verify faculty , staff and necessary instructional 
facilities, required as per provisions of V Dean’s Committee Report, land use pattern 
etc. during the period. Based on the report of Mid -Term Review Comm ittee 
subsequent accreditation of the programme  for another four years period may be 
considered. Accordingly, the appeal is disposed-off.  
 
1.2.5. B.Sc. (Hons) Agriculture programme of Khalsa College, Amritsar  
 
Examination of documents and discussion by Appeal Committee: Appeal 
Committee examined the  appeal document submitted by the College, Self-Study 
Report, PRT report, additional documents submitted by the University , especially 
ITR forms, land records and further held discussion with PRT Chairman, Member 
Secretary and College Principal/other officers. Appeal Committee noted that 
University was also approved by Punjab Council for 240 seats in B. Sc. (Hons.) 
Agriculture Programme, but could not maintain the commensurate instructional 
facilities and faculty for this intake. During PRT visit infrastructure and faculty 
available with the college was not matching with intake of 240. 
  
Recommendation: Considering the reports, documents and discussion mentioned 
above, Appeal Committee did not recommend considering acc reditation of the B. 
Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture programme on the ground that PRT on its own cannot 
increase or reduce student intake. College may resubmit application for accreditation 
to ICAR after either creating matching instructional facilities with prese nt student 
intake or with reduced intake with existing facilities. Accordingly, the appeal is 
disposed-off.  
  
1.2.6. M.Sc. (Agri) and Ph.D. degree programme in Plant Pathology, College of 
Agriculture, KSNUAHS, Shivamogga 
Examination of documents and discussion by Appeal Committee : The Appeal 
Committee examined the  Appeal document,  Self-Study Report, PRT report, 
additional documents submitted by the University and held discussion with PRT 
Chairman, Member Secretary and University Vice -Chancellor/Former Vice -
Chancellor. Appeal Committee noted that Department of Plant Pathology has 
sufficient staff and instructional facilities to run the degree programmes. Committee 
further noted that PRT has made errors in its report while making assessment and 
scoring.  
 
Recommendation: Considering the reports, documents and discussion mentioned 
above, appeal committee recommended considering accreditation of M. Sc. (Agri) 
and Ph. D. Plant Pathology programmes in College of Agriculture for a period of 
five years which will be co-terminus with university accreditation.  
 
1.2.6. General Recommendations by Appeal Committee : During examination of 
documents, the Appeal Committee made certain recommendations as below:  
 
5 
 
 Member Secretaries should be sensitized enough to advise PRTs for presenting facts 
and figures and preparing assessment as per guidelines and instructions issued by 
the Board from time to time. Generalized and ambiguous nature of observations, 
which are creating problems during verification and examination of SSRs, should be 
strictly avoided.  
 Staggered timing should be allotted to the Universities and PRTs during Appeal 
Committee meetings and timeline should be adhered.  
 Copy of accreditation notification and/or certificate should be provided to the 
Appeal Committee members for the cases under its consideration.  
 After approval of the Board, score card may be provided to the Universities.  
 The prescribed faculty strength needs a review. Besides a critical l imit for 
accreditation need to be fixed because PRTs follow the written prescription. It has 
been suggested that 60% of positions filled at all times could be considered as critical 
(minimum) for accreditation. Suggestive scoring could be 60-69% 2; 70-79% 3; and 
80% plus-4 marks. This is likely to bring more objective marking.   
 Appeal Committee was critical for framing minimum requirements for programmes, 
especially with respect to intake of students. In case of multiple number of intakes 
over and above th at mentioned in book of Minimum Requirement for Establishing 
of Agricultural Colleges, proportional increase in infrastructure and facilities and 
faculty should be suggested. Faculty guidelines for Departments, commensurate 
with intake should be developed for Post Graduate and Ph.D. programmes. 
 Sufficient time period should be given to PRTs for on-spot verification of SSRs. 
 
Observation of the Board: Board discussed above specific recommendations of the 
Appeal Committee and directed to bring these issues in the pertinent committee for 
further discussion and consideration.

3.6 Specific issues with the permission of the Chair 
3.6.1. Uniformity in PRT report preparation 
Considering large number of applications for accreditation,  especially from Private 
Universities/Colleges, it is now required to develop uniform PRT reports. Many a times 
it has been noticed that the representatives of the NAEAB in Peer Review Teams 
(Member Secretaries) are not able to guide the PRT properly or of fer different 
interpretations for facts and figures either in SSRs or supplementary evidences being 
made available by the Universities. In order to avoid multiple interpretations and 
circumstantial inferences being drawn, there is need to suggest uniform p roforma for 
report presentations for the degree programmes (Annexure -I). The said proforma has 
been generated considering guidelines and feedback received from PRT reports. 
Proforma was presented in the Board  which was approved in principle. I t was suggested to 
circulate proforma among Board Members and modify if some suggestions are received.  
 
3.6.2. Segregation of Essential Criteria and General Guidelines for accreditation.  
Presently, during the process of accreditation, Letter of Intent, Institutional Eligibility for 
Accreditation and Statement of Compliance are submitted  by applicant Universities 
through accreditation portal. These three documents were co -opted from NAAC during 
2017, while introducing scoring/grading system in accreditation, to receive background 
information about universities prior to submission of Self Study Report. Over the time, 
it has been realized that proper customization of Letter of Intent and Institutional 
Eligibility for Accreditation in the line of educational require ments in agriculture and 
allied sciences is need of the hour.  
Since ICAR is not an approving body for agricultural colleges, as it does not has statutory 
authority, h owever, it is required to ensure  Minimum Requirements for Establishing 
28 
 
Agricultural Colleges, specifically  instructional facilities  including farm and course 
specific units  and staff prior to submission of Self Study Reports during process of 
accreditation. Considering this fact, NAEAB has been assigned dual responsibility of 
ensuring minimum requirement at first and then conducting accreditation for assessment 
of teaching/learning process thereafter. These two parts of accreditation process need to 
be segregated  
Further, essential criteria for accreditation is to be defined and to be segregated from Self 
Study Reports, which is considered as core document for accreditation . The basic issue 
need to be considered here that Self Study Reports and subsequent Peer Review Reports 
should avoid discussion on essential requirements for Departments , Colleges and the 
Agricultural University. Rather, the focus of Peer Review Teams should be completely 
on implementation of standard teaching/learning process, monitoring mechanism, 
establishment and functioning of authorities as specified by the Council time to time  
through Guidelines.  
Considering above facts, a new format of Letter of Intent (Annexure-II) and Institutional 
Eligibility for Accreditation (Annexure -III) were presented was approved in principle , 
however, need further deliberations.  It was suggested to circulate proforma among Board 
Members and modify if some suggestions are received.
